key_terms: An Atlas label, optionally with attributes, attached to entities. Its meaning, owner and review process must be defined outside the string.
Finding entities by type, classification or attribute through Atlas's search index rather than by GUID.
The delay between a successful mutation and its appearance in search results while direct GUID reads already show it.
Atlas's option to pass a classification along lineage to downstream entities.
The data-access boundary, such as a query engine authorizer, that must map a classification to a policy for any access to be denied.

worked_examples.title: Define and attach a review classification
worked_examples.interpretation: The classification type must exist before any entity can carry it, which is why apply creates missing typedefs first and refuses to alter an existing one with different super types. The curated entity then lists the label under classifications. A classification is a statement that someone reviewed the asset; it does not change who can read the data unless a separate policy engine acts on it.

worked_examples.title: Find assets by label, then remove one label
worked_examples.interpretation: Basic search goes through the search index, so a label attached a moment ago may not appear yet even though reading the entity by GUID already shows it. After the DELETE, the entity should remain ACTIVE with an empty classifications list; only the label is gone. If the entity itself disappears, the wrong endpoint was called. Poll search with a deadline before concluding the index is wrong.

evidence: Complete real Atlas REST payload/client route with default local server omitted. Native compatible server preparation and actual API/graph/index/lifecycle acceptance are explicit separate work, never simulated execution.
